title: Check resources out of a pool of 10 and return them, from many callers
summary: A pool of 10 reusable resources; 12 to 64 concurrent callers each check one out, touch it, yield once while holding it, and return it, 100 to 4,800 cycles in all.
notes: An asynchronous task on one thread: each operation is one call that ends when every caller has finished its cycles and the pool has been emptied again. A cycle only checks out, touches, yields once and returns, so the figure is the pool's bookkeeping and the runtime's scheduling of callers waiting for a resource, not work in the cycles. The pool and the callers are created inside the call. Go runs with GOMAXPROCS=1, Rust on tokio's current-thread runtime, Python on one asyncio loop; Ruby has no event loop in its standard library and uses threads, which take turns under the interpreter lock.
